precepts.text: There is history behind why Paul said let the women keep silence in the churches. In Ephesus and that whole region around Corinth they worshipped the great goddess Diana, whom all Asia and the world worshipped, and the people cried out for two hours, Great is Diana of the Ephesians. Some of those women repented, so to speak, came into the church, and brought that goddess spirit with them. That whole feminist movement is the same spirit back today.
precepts.point: Whenever you are having these issues in your household, it is because you allowed confusion to breach. You allowed feminism in the house; you did not stop it at the door. You allowed pride to come in.
precepts.why:
“For God is not the author of confusion, but of peace, as in all churches of the saints. Let your women keep silence in the churches”. Why does that follow right after God is not the author of confusion? Because a woman speaking out of turn concerning the church is confusion. A woman not being in order is confusion.

There is history behind why Paul said to let the women keep silence in the churches. Acts 19: “And it came to pass, that, while Apollos was at Corinth, Paul having passed through the upper coasts came to Ephesus”. This is what was happening in that whole region of Corinth and Ephesus.

The craftsmen feared “that the temple of the great goddess Diana should be despised, and her magnificence should be destroyed, whom all Asia and the world worshippeth.” Who were they worshipping? The great goddess Diana. And when they knew Paul was a Jew, “all with one voice about the space of two hours cried out, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.”

That goddess worship ran through Corinth and that whole area. Some of those women repented, so to speak, came into the church, and brought that goddess spirit with them. That whole feminist movement is the same spirit, back today, and sisters do not want to admit that is the spirit they are rolling in. Feminism has been normalized to where a man has to whisper in his own house.

So when there are issues in your household, it is because you allowed confusion to breach: you let feminism and pride in and did not stop them at the door. If you are scared of your wife, brother, take the purple shirt off; you cannot cast down the lies of the nations and bring us out of captivity if you are scared to deal with your wife at home. The head of every man is Christ, and the head of the woman is the man; that is the divine order, and God is not the author of confusion.

precepts.text: I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.
precepts.point: Demetrius the silversmith made shrines for Diana and stirred up the craftsmen because Paul had persuaded much people that they be no gods which are made with hands, endangering both their wealth and the temple of the great goddess whom all Asia worshipped.
precepts.why:
“And the same time there arose no small stir about that way.” What way is this? Christ answers it: “I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.” The way that Ephesus was stirred up about, the thing that caused a huge commotion in that city, was Christ himself.

They had a problem with Christ because a whole city was given to witchcraft. Ephesus owed its fame to the temple of Diana, and the “curious arts” practised there were the magical arts of the Ephesian conjurers. When Paul came preaching Christ, “many that believed came, and confessed, and shewed their deeds”, and those who used curious arts brought their books of witchcraft together and burned them before all men, fifty thousand pieces of silver worth. “So mightily grew the word of God and prevailed.”

That is what stirred the city. Demetrius the silversmith, “which made silver shrines for Diana”, called the craftsmen together and told them “by this craft we have our wealth”, and that Paul had “persuaded and turned away much people, saying that they be no gods, which are made with hands.” People were repenting and turning away from their witchcraft, and that put both the craftsmen’s living and the temple of “the great goddess Diana” in danger. Diana, with all the breasts on her, goes into fertility: satanic worship at the end of the day.

So the stir “about that way” was a city given over to idolatry and sorcery fighting against Christ, the only way to the Father. There is no salvation without him, and the same call goes out to our people now: repent from the idolatry, the fornication and the lasciviousness, and come to the way.

precepts.why: “Moreover ye see and hear, that not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul hath persuaded and turned away much people, saying that they be no gods, which are made with hands:” So what does that prove? That sometime later the spirit said to Paul and them, now it's time to preach throughout Asia. But what we read in Acts 16, at that time the Holy Ghost said do not go there, now is not the time, there's nobody going to wake up at that time; the spirit said you have to wait till later.

precepts.why: Of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus: you have people that came out of Asia that believed. “And this continued by the space of two years; so that all they which dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks.” Jews and Greeks. When you read the term Greeks, most Christians will say, see, it is for all nations. But 2 Maccabees 4 shows what the Bible says about the Greeks.

points: This continued by the space of two years, so that all they which dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks. That means Colosse heard the word Paul was preaching. You will not find a verse in Acts saying Paul went to Colosse, but we actually did just read it, because Colosse is in Asia next to Ephesus. If you always wondered why you cannot find the precept in Acts, that is your precept right there.

points: Not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul hath persuaded and turned away much people. Turned them away from idolatry to serving the one true God and believing on Jesus the Christ.

points: The temple of the great goddess Diana, whom all Asia and the world worshipped. Colosse, just like Ephesus, just like the rest of the world, was worshipping Diana. They worshipped these women deities, just like America worships the Virgin Mary, women's rights, liberation, all of that. It is the same thing. But the spirit was so heavy on the apostle Paul that places he did not physically go to were getting touched.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

points: Many that believed confessed their deeds, and many which used curious arts brought their books and burned them, worth fifty thousand pieces of silver. Curious arts are the magical arts of the Ephesian conjurers: witchcraft was what the city was known for.
Timotheus who ministered to Paul here is the Timothy of the epistles. Then arose no small stir about that way, and the way is Christ, whom a city given to witchcraft had a problem with.

Demetrius the silversmith made shrines for Diana and stirred up the craftsmen because Paul had persuaded much people that they be no gods which are made with hands, endangering both their wealth and the temple of the great goddess whom all Asia worshipped.

The Greco-Roman world the gospel entered was a tough pagan environment where ritual worship of Diana involved sexual immorality, drunkenness and orgies. That is the lifestyle the Ephesians came out of.

Diana of the Ephesians is depicted covered in breasts, a fertility goddess like Baal. When they knew Paul's companion was a Jew, the whole theater cried 'Great is Diana of the Ephesians' for two hours.
